post.yt_title: Hasn't the Bible Been Changed Over Time? 📜 #shorts
post.yt_desc:
"Hasn't the Bible been changed so many times we can't trust it?" Fair question. The Great Isaiah Scroll from the Dead Sea Scrolls is about a thousand years older than the oldest Hebrew copies of Isaiah we had before 1947, and it reads almost the same.

"The grass withers, the flower fades, But the word of our God stands forever" (Isaiah 40:8 NKJV).

The New Testament? Over five thousand Greek manuscripts to compare. Jesus said, "Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will by no means pass away" (Matthew 24:35 NKJV).

📖 Read it yourself: Isaiah 40:6–8 · Matthew 24:35 (NKJV)

post.notes:
- Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a), found 1947 at Qumran, dated c. 150–100 BC (some say c. 125 BC). Before it, the oldest complete Hebrew Isaiah texts were medieval Masoretic manuscripts (Aleppo Codex c. AD 930; Leningrad Codex AD 1008): about 1,000 years apart.
- 'Almost the same': differences are mostly spelling and small variants; the standard scholarly summary is substantial agreement with the Masoretic Text.
- Over 5,000 Greek New Testament manuscripts (catalogued count is about 5,800).
- Isaiah 40:8 NKJV quoted in full (NKJV capitalizes "But" as a poetic line; scroll keeps it).
- Matthew 24:35 NKJV quoted in full.
